analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (Nov 6, 2026)
key_insights: Futures are up led by Tech after the market's worst day since 'Liberation Day', which was driven by residual AI fears and the midterm elections as a catalyst. Semis and Memory are retracing about 30%-40% of yesterday's losses, and Mag7 and Software are also bid.
Yesterday saw $1.74T in trading value, the highest since the June 26 rebalance. JPM's derivatives desk was very busy in VIX downside.

The open question for the day is whether the relief rally holds or whether selling and de-risking resume into the weekend. JPM says NFP may carry asymmetric downside risk: a beat is backward looking, and a miss would add to recession fears tied to 'if AI fails or capex goes to zero'.

European and Asian markets fell sharply: UKX -2.0%, SX5E -1.5%, DAX -2.1%, NKY -6.0%, KOSPI -6.0%. European baskets show buyers of Semis, Renewables and Mideast shorts, while Software, Defense and Luxury are under pressure.

Ron Adler (Equity HT Cash Trading) calls AI the fulcrum of the market. Hyperscalers began funding ambitions via capital markets rather than capex, which pushed traders further out the risk curve into picks-and-shovels names. He cites META raising money at 7.5%, a Chinese chipmaker putting its IPO on hold, MRVL down about 40% after the LITE deal announcement, and hedge fund stress.

Adler says the midterms were one of two clearing events left for the year and that many took them as a signal for broader risk-on. He says the election will make datacenter growth harder, which is hitting Photonics/Optics, Memory and neoclouds.

Crowding remains a pain point. HF long/short spreads are working today. JPM volumes are +50% after a busy post-election session, with client questions on pain levels, unwinding and fund stress multiplying. Adler does not expect many to rush in to defend outside of defensives.

Adler says the flows look directionally rational but the magnitude is surprising. He says much of the positioning pain has been taken, and that a harder path for datacenter expansion could ease pressure on capital markets and yields.
Feroli expects NFP of +75k vs the Street's 65k and a prior of 29k. He expects unemployment at 4.1% vs 4.2% prior and average hourly earnings of +0.20% MoM and +2.8% YoY, a new cycle low.
Same-day options priced about a 0.9% move at the open, rising to about 1.6% by 1:30pm.
Retail investors sold nearly $1.3bn by 12pm, a -6.2z event, concentrated in Mag7, Semis and levered ETFs. Brian Heaven's desk cites a -7.2z retail selling event.

Mark Schilsky (TMT) says SOXX fell 9% with nowhere to hide: Megas, Internet and Software (Infra and Cyber more than App Software) were all down. He questions whether it was de-grossing, since popular shorts did not rally, and suggests retail may have given up on the AI trade.

Brian Heavey (TMT) says SOXX is trading like a full stop-out, SMH broke through its 200-day average, and semi charts could test the April 1 levels. He says the hyperscaler gains the day before reversed, and that a harder political backdrop for datacenter buildouts hurts what was the sole driver of US GDP growth.
Brendan Henrici (Energy/Mats/Utils) says gold outperformed the S&P by 5%, the largest gap since February, so gold is acting as a safe haven again just as CTAs got short.

Henrici says volume in the JP1XVOLT grid/AI power basket was 230m shares yesterday and tracking 300m today, more than 500m over two days. That exceeds any two-day period in 3 years and DeepSeek's ~320m max. The basket had its largest two-day drawdown (16%) since March 2020, which he calls capitulatory.

Briggs Barton (Consumer) says Retail faded about 300bps vs Staples up about 100bps. Demand is tilting to quality (VIK, LTH) and to defensives and inflation plays (ORLY, AZO, TSCO), with large-cap staples bid (WMT, COST, KO, KDP).

JPM's US Market Intel view stays Tactically Bullish and expects a Tech rebound. Positioning Intel finds that when the NDX is within ~6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5%+, it rebounds about 3% the following week, with a stronger effect if the drop is on a Friday.

JPM argues that a US recession from an AI capex decline is unlikely. Its reasons are record household net worth and strong cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant hiring driver. CRWV employs 550 people. The main effects would be lower capex (GDP) and possible hyperscaler layoffs.

JPM sees the biggest non-AI risk as a re-escalation in the Middle East. Iran damaged US regional bases and US munition levels are depleted, which may point to diplomacy. Oil already appears to price another attack, so JPM sees limited upside for energy, yields and downside for equities.
Seasonality: November has been the strongest month on average this century, and post-midterm seasonality is also a tailwind.

Monetization Menu (Nov 2): expects broadening to continue with a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals, playing a tactical Tech rebound. Favors Consumers and Financials if the curve steepens, and Europe if US/Iran move toward a deal. In Jan-Feb, US Value was +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.
Prior menus: Oct 26 suggested adding hedges via long oil/Energy equities and long vol. Oct 19 favored Tech, pairs trades and derivatives, Financials and Retailers, and Brazil and Japan.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM stays Tactically Bullish. After a Friday flush the NDX tends to rebound ~3% the following week, the positioning pain has largely been taken, and November and post-midterm seasonality are tailwinds.
tension_points.bear_case: Crowding, fund stress and a negative feedback loop in the AI datacenter trade, with capital markets appearing to close, could bring more de-risking into the weekend. NFP carries asymmetric downside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An NFP miss that adds to recession fears, or SMH retesting the April 1 levels after breaking the 200-day average.

tension_points.theme: AI capex decline and US recession
tension_points.bull_case: Record household net worth, strong cash, record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant hiring driver mean capex cuts hit GDP but not labor or spending.
tension_points.bear_case: Recessionary fears are part of the narrative if AI fails or capex goes to zero, and a bear market would create a negative wealth effect.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Margins compressing enough to trigger mass layoffs.
